items.title: Czech scientists detect lightning on Mars from orbit for the first time

featured_image.name: Listen to the crackle of Martian 'mini-lightning'

items.description: A team of Czech scientists has identified a lightning-generated radio signal in data from NASA's MAVEN spacecraft, providing the first orbital evidence of electrical discharge activity in the Martian atmosphere. The finding, published February 27 in the journal Science Advances, adds a new dimension to the growing body of evidence that Mars is an electrically active world.[1][2]

items.title: Pentagon labels Anthropic a supply chain risk after AI safety standoff

featured_image.name: Hegseth declares Anthropic a "supply chain risk to national ...

items.description:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Friday designated AI company Anthropic a supply chain risk to national security, barring military contractors from doing business with the company after its CEO refused to lift safeguards on the use of its technology for mass domestic surveillance and fully autonomous weapons.

The move came shortly after President Trump ordered all federal agencies to "immediately cease" using Anthropic's technology. "We don't need it, we don't want it, and will not do business with them again!" Trump wrote on Truth Social, though he allowed a six-month phase-out period for the Defense Department and other agencies currently relying on the company's products.[1][2]

items.title: Chile bars Chinese hospital ship from treating locals amid US pressure

featured_image.name: Chile denies onboard care by Chinese medical ship as US ...

items.description:
Chile has refused to allow a Chinese hospital ship to provide medical services to local residents onboard, citing a lack of proper authorization, in a decision that underscores the growing geopolitical tug-of-war between Washington and Beijing across Latin America.

The medical vessel Silk Road Ark, currently on a voyage to roughly a dozen countries as part of China's "Mission Harmony 2025," arrived in waters off the Chilean port city of Valparaiso on Wednesday, according to Reuters. Chile's Ministry of Health said it had been reviewing a request submitted through the foreign ministry at the end of 2025 for the ship to offer medical care to locals, but ultimately declined. "We determined that it is not appropriate to authorize this health operation to function on the ship's facilities," the ministry said, pointing to a local health code that restricts such services to professionals accredited in the country.[1][2]

items.title: Ghana says 55 citizens killed fighting for Russia in Ukraine

featured_image.name: Ghana says at least 55 of its people killed after Russia 'lured' them to ...

items.description:
At least 55 Ghanaians have died fighting for Russia in Ukraine after being recruited through criminal trafficking networks, Ghana's Foreign Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa said on Friday, marking one of the highest confirmed death tolls among African nations whose citizens have been drawn into the conflict.[1][2]

Ablakwa, who shared the figures on the social media platform X following high-level talks in Kyiv, said Ukrainian intelligence had documented 272 Ghanaians lured into the war since 2022, with two currently held as prisoners of war. "Ukrainian authorities revealed that from their credible intelligence gathering, they have documented 1,780 Africans from 36 countries who have been lured by criminal trafficking networks to join the war against Ukraine," Ablakwa said.[3][1]

items.title: Britain withdraws embassy staff from Iran amid US military buildup

featured_image.name: Starmer ‘supporting’ US-Iran talks after Trump threatens military action

items.description:
Britain withdrew its diplomatic staff from Iran and relocated embassy personnel inside Israel on Friday as a standoff with Washington over the use of the Diego Garcia military base deepened against a backdrop of faltering US-Iran nuclear negotiations and a massive American military buildup in the Middle East.

The White House is refusing to back the UK's agreement to hand sovereignty of the Chagos Islands to Mauritius unless Prime Minister Keir Starmer allows the United States to use the jointly operated Diego Garcia base for potential strikes on Iran, according to Whitehall sources cited by GB News. Downing Street has so far resisted, with British officials arguing that permitting such an operation would violate international law.[1][2][3]

items.title: Fico says Ukraine has 'no interest' in restoring Druzhba oil pipeline after call with Zelenskyy

featured_image.name: Slovakia threatens to cut electricity to Ukraine over Russian oil spat

items.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico spoke by phone on Friday as a monthlong dispute over disrupted Russian oil supplies through the Druzhba pipeline showed no signs of resolution, with the standoff now blocking billions in EU financial aid to Kyiv and a new package of sanctions against Moscow.

Zelenskyy invited Fico to visit Ukraine to discuss "all issues" in person, according to a statement from the Ukrainian presidential office. Fico said he accepted the proposal for a meeting but would prefer it take place in an EU member state rather than in Ukraine. He offered a blunt assessment of the call: "I had the distinct impression that Ukraine has no interest in restoring oil transit through its territory."[1][2][3]

items.title: Meloni calls Trump tariffs a 'mistake,' proposes EU-US free-trade zone

featured_image.name: Italy's PM Meloni calls Trump's Greenland tariffs on Europe a mistake

items.description:
In an interview with Bloomberg published Friday, Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni called for the European Union to form a free-trade zone with the United States, an ambitious proposal aimed at resolving the transatlantic tariff standoff that has rattled markets and stalled trade policy on both sides of the Atlantic.[1][2]

Meloni described President Donald Trump's tariffs as a "mistake" and urged the EU to move forward with adopting the trade agreement it struck with Washington last summer, known as the Turnberry deal, according to Bloomberg. The deal, reached at Trump's Scottish golf resort in July 2025, set a 15% ceiling on tariffs for most EU exports to the United States in exchange for the EU eliminating import duties on all US industrial goods.[3][4][5][1]

items.title: Taliban signal willingness to talk after Pakistan launches airstrikes

featured_image.name: Pakistan says ‘patience has run out' as it bombs Taliban across Afghanistan

items.description:
Afghanistan's Taliban government said Friday it was open to negotiations with Pakistan, even as the two nations exchanged their most serious cross-border attacks in years. The diplomatic overture came hours after Pakistan launched airstrikes on Kabul, Kandahar, and Paktia province, with its defense minister declaring that the countries are now in a state of "open war."[1][2][3]

The conflicting signals — a willingness to talk paired with escalating military operations — underscore the volatile and rapidly shifting dynamics between the once-allied neighbors, whose relationship has deteriorated sharply over Pakistan's accusations that the Taliban harbors militant groups responsible for attacks inside Pakistani territory.

items.title: Trump warns of military force against Iran as nuclear talks stall

featured_image.name: Trump's claim on Iranian missile development said ...

items.description:
President Donald Trump on Friday expressed frustration with the progress of nuclear negotiations with Iran and warned that military force remains on the table, telling reporters, "Don't want to, but sometimes you have to," when asked whether he would order strikes against the Islamic Republic.[1][2]

Speaking to reporters before departing the White House for a trip to Texas, Trump said he was "not happy" with Iran's posture in the talks and reiterated his core demand. "I'm not happy with the fact that they're not willing to give us what we have to have. I'm not thrilled with that," he said, adding: "Iran cannot have nuclear weapons".[3][4]
